original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: For the exact 36 E6 root lines in the pinned E8 realization, exhaust all 70 principal and 4,900 ordered four-coordinate projected-Gram decoders M=P_U P_V^T. Price the entrywise-maximal symmetric compatible pairing B, and certify whether any candidate reaches Theorem C cost 22. For the 13 full-rank, nonzero-diagonal candidates, also certify that no rank-five Gram pairing B=A A^T over F2^5 satisfies the forced-zero graph.
scope_change_reason: The assigned complex rank-shape card normally prices the selected complex word, but the current selector suggested a broad decoder route and the live handoff offered an unclaimed E6 low-T construction question. This package tests one new concrete rank-four projected-Gram family with a decoder-adapted pairing. It does not map into the selected provider or transfer a kappa.
bottleneck_link: A cost-at-most-22 E6 T=4 decoder would meet the local h=9 break-even threshold and test a larger-child decoder mechanism. The result remains a root-unit local construction question; selected-provider placement and any global exponent transfer are not established.
stop_rule: Exhaust the 70 principal projections, then all 4,900 ordered four-coordinate pairs if no principal candidate reaches cost 22. Build an exact six-clique witness for every full-rank nonzero-diagonal candidate to test the rank-five Gram-pairing subfamily. Stop after these finite domains; do not expand to arbitrary rational coefficient matrices or arbitrary pairings in this cycle.
evidence: verify.py exactly regenerates 36 E6 lines and exhausts 70 principal plus 4,900 ordered projections. Only 13 ordered candidates have rank-four factors and nonzero diagonal; the minimum charge under the maximal compatible pairing is 65, at U=[3,4,5,6], V=[3,4,5,7]. Every one of the 13 required-zero graphs contains a certified six-clique, excluding a rank-five Gram pairing because six norm-one mutually orthogonal vectors cannot lie in F2^5. This is not a lower bound for sparser non-Gram pairings or arbitrary E6 decoders.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in the exact construction, search, proof certificate, verifier, and writing. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can one of the 13 projected-Gram decoders use a rank-six or higher admissible pairing whose four restricted support blocks have total charged cost at most 22?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact screen excludes only the entrywise-maximal pairing and rank-five Gram pairings; a remaining low-cost sparse pairing could still meet the E6 h=9 window.
open_questions.first_step: For the best candidate U=[3,4,5,6], V=[3,4,5,7], encode one shared symmetric B on the allowed zero pairs and exact upper bounds on the four block ranks, beginning with rank pattern (5,5,6,6).
open_questions.blocked_by: A complete search over arbitrary admissible B is a coupled binary matrix-rank problem and was not run in this package.

open_questions.question: Can an E6 rank-four rational decoder outside the four-coordinate projected-Gram family meet the same threshold?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Any positive answer would supply a materially different low-T block; PR #2137 covers only the fixed-B0 coordinate-bilinear family.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one structured non-coordinate factor family and derive its fully charged local E6 cost before synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not search arbitrary rational coefficients or give a mapping into the selected provider.
